conceptZh: 自以為藏得很好的布忍者被提早爆開的煙霧彈彈得四處反跳，每次撞擊都敲定一筆「丘」，最後得意坐上字頂，再跳到小山丘後露出整顆頭。
object: Five solid teal stroke pieces and a small rounded grassy hill.
morph: Five ricochet impacts seat five rigid pieces into the exact five-stroke structure of 丘.
creativeAngle: 把忍者藏身失敗變成五次反彈的連鎖笑點，以撞擊逐筆敲出正確字形；最後用遮不住忍者的小山丘呼應詞義。
promptEn:
Create an 8-second stylized stop-motion-style cartoon with tactile felt and painted wooden pieces. A tiny plum-colored felt ninja has embroidered eyebrows, stubby limbs and enormous confidence in his terrible hiding skills. Use a pale warm-peach stage, soft light and a locked frontal camera. Five saturated teal wooden stroke pieces await assembly at center; a tiny rounded grassy hill sits at the far right. Invisible elastic stage boundaries provide the rebounds. No other cast.

0.00–1.10: The ninja points at the hill, determined to hide behind it, then tiptoes conspicuously across the open stage with his eyes squeezed shut. The first off-screen “丘” accompanies the beginning of the build: he pulls the short slanting stroke toward its assembly position with his foot. His felt smoke bomb prematurely gives one soft puff beneath him, launching him sideways; the puff clears immediately.

1.10–2.70: A floor bounce makes his padded heel CLACK the short slanting stroke into place. He rebounds off the left boundary, belly-bonking the upper horizontal into position, then pinballs off the ceiling to seat the left vertical. Each impact visibly drives one piece along a short straight path into its final location. His smug expression becomes a wide-eyed wobble; keep his whole trajectory visible.

2.70–5.00: He ricochets from the right boundary and knocks in the inner vertical. One bigger, harmless bottom-first floor BONK sends the long bottom horizontal sliding home with a satisfying soft wooden clack, completing 丘 by 4.30. Speak the second “丘” during this final assembly. The recoil drops him sitting proudly on the glyph’s upper edge for a brief dizzy grin; he immediately springs clear and lands beside the grassy hill by 5.00. Preserve the exact standard Traditional Chinese structure of 丘 throughout assembly: five distinct strokes, correct connections and proportions, no rounded substitutions.

5.00–8.00: Hold the completed 丘 perfectly still, centered, uncropped, approximately 70% of frame height with clear margins. At 5.35–6.55, speak “山丘” exactly as the ninja pats the visibly rounded grassy hill and ducks behind it. His entire oversized felt head remains visible above its summit; convinced he has vanished, he gives a silent triumphant eyebrow wiggle. Keep this small action in the side margin, clear of every stroke.

Audio: warm, friendly off-screen Taiwanese Mandarin, reading exactly “丘、丘、山丘” (ㄑㄧㄡ、ㄑㄧㄡ、ㄕㄢ ㄑㄧㄡ), slowly and distinctly with accurate tones and short pauses. Stop after the word. Use gentle bounce squeaks and soft clacks beneath the voice. The single target glyph 丘 is the only on-screen text; no subtitles, logos, watermark, flashing effects or extra dialogue.
